The fourth is named the Ground of the Power of Wisdom that Acts through the Merit of Pure and Wondrous Golden Light.
The fifth is named the Ground of the Illumination of the Treasury of Majestic Power in the Field of the Flavor of Radiance.
The sixth is named the Ground of the Blazing Torch that Opens the Blooming, Supreme, Pure, and Stainless in Space.
The seventh is named the Ground of the Arising of Light from the Treasury of the Vast Dharma Realm.

The eighth is named the Ground of the Pervasive Illumination of the Light of the Most Supreme, Wondrously Pure Buddha-Wisdom Treasury, Which Purifies All Obstructions through the Supernormal Knowledge of Wisdom.
The ninth is named the Ground of the Vairocana-Light Produced by Billions of Boundless Adorned Vows.
The tenth is named the Vairocana Stage of the Ocean of Wisdom.
O Noble Being!
These are called the ten stages of the ineffable wisdom of the Tathāgata.
"In the first stage of the Tathāgata, all subtle habitual tendencies are completely and correctly severed, and he possesses sovereign mastery and unimpededness regarding all phenomena.
In the second stage of the Tathāgata, he turns the wheel of the true Dharma to manifest the profoundly deep teachings."
In the third stage of the Tathāgata, he establishes the teachings and precepts for śrāvakas and ordains the three vehicles.
In the fourth stage of the Tathāgata, he expounds the eighty-four thousand aggregates of Dharma to subdue the four māras.
In the fifth stage of the Tathāgata, he crushes all heterodox arguments and their false teachings, and subdues all those who practice evil paths.

In the sixth stage of the Tathāgata, he establishes boundless sentient beings in the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) and the six great penetrations (*ṣaḍabhijñā*), namely: manifesting boundless Buddha-lands adorned with purity by means of the Buddha’s merits;
and manifesting boundless bodhisattvas attending and surrounding him.
He manifests Buddha-lands as vast and boundless;
he manifests his own body appearing within boundless Buddha-lands;
and he manifests passing into parinirvāṇa, even to the point of the disappearance of the Dharma.
He manifests boundless supernormal powers, spiritual transformations, and miraculous displays.

Because the seven factors of enlightenment on the seventh stage of the Tathāgata are devoid of intrinsic nature and free from attachment, he reveals them to all bodhisattvas in accordance with reality.
In the eighth stage, the Tathāgata bestows the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* upon all bodhisattvas by means of the four methods of answering questions.
In the ninth stage, the Tathāgata demonstrates to all bodhisattvas through skillful means.

In the ten stages of the Tathāgata, by means of the teaching that all dharmas are without intrinsic nature, he instructs all bodhisattvas; he utters the sound of Great Parinirvāṇa and proclaims that all dharmas are ultimately in a state of parinirvāṇa.
When these ten stages of the Tathāgata were being proclaimed, from this Sahā buddha-field to unspeakably many buddha-fields throughout the ten directions, eighteen great omens appeared everywhere:

namely, shaking, great shaking, and universal shaking; trembling, great trembling, and universal trembling; rolling, great rolling, and universal rolling; sounding, great sounding, and universal sounding; roaring, great roaring, and universal roaring; and crashing, great crashing, and universal crashing.

All Buddha-lands surged up in the east and sank in the west; they surged up in the west and sank in the east; they surged up in the south and sank in the north; they surged up in the north and sank in the south; they surged up in the center and sank at the periphery; and they surged up at the periphery and sank in the center.
In all Buddha-lands, the twelve marks of transformation appear; yet all sentient beings therein are free from fear or harm and are entirely at peace.
Great radiance is emitted from all Buddha-lands, so that even the deepest darkness, the most obscure regions, and the intervals between worlds are all brilliantly illuminated.
Furthermore, all worlds—whether in the process of formation or destruction, whether possessing a Buddha or lacking one—all manifest within this land.
Celestial flowers of exquisite beauty rained down everywhere throughout the unspeakably many and boundless buddha-fields of the ten directions, namely:
māndārava flowers, mahāmāndārava flowers, mañjūṣaka flowers, mahāmañjūṣaka flowers, light flowers, great light flowers, moon flowers, and great moon flowers.
Furthermore, throughout all Buddha-fields, all musical instruments began to play spontaneously without being struck, and everywhere there appeared great, unprecedented phenomena.

In all Buddha-fields, the personal attendants of the Buddhas rose from their seats and each questioned their own Buddha regarding this great, marvelous, and unprecedented phenomenon; each Buddha then explained it in detail in response to their questions.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Sāgaravaradharagambhīravikrīḍitājñānābhijña and the rest were seated in the Palace Adorned with Jewels; the entire assembly of bodhisattvas all marveled in astonishment, saying:

"The sphere of the profound Tathāgatas traversed by the Buddhas is supreme, difficult to know, subtle, and difficult to see; it is beyond the reach of all bodhisattvas, let alone śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas."

Why is this? This inconceivable tenfold stage of the Tathāgata is something we have never heard before; we should now together entreat the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, to explain its meaning in detail.
Then, the bodhisattvas each rose from their seats, bowed with palms joined, and requested in verse:
"O Peerless World-Honored One, Supreme Victor!
Please proclaim the names of the various Buddha-grounds."
Never before have we heard such a thing—unparalleled and supreme.
With a single mind of exultation, we entreat you to extensively expound the meaning of the stages;
as the hungry longs for exquisite food, and the thirsty craves delicious drink.
"May the Buddha universally bestow his compassion and fully expound the stages of the Tathāgata.
Having thus requested the Buddha in verse, the assembly of bodhisattvas circumambulated him three times to the right, prostrated at his feet, and each withdrew to sit upon a lotus throne.

At that time, the World-Honored One, having performed the lion-stretch and surveyed the ten directions, addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaravaradharagambhīravikrīḍitājñānābhijña, saying: “Noble Son!

The meaning of the Tathāgata-stage is most supreme, profound, and subtle; it is difficult to recognize, difficult to enter, and difficult to awaken to. It is not an object of language, transcending all sounds and discursive explanations.
Why is this? Since even the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas cannot be described, how much less can the stages of the bodhisattvas or the stage of the Tathāgata be expressed in words?
The Bodhisattva Sāgaravaradharagambhīravikrīḍitājñānābhijña addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How many stages of the Śrāvaka are there?”
The Buddha said:
"There are ten stages of the śrāvaka. They are as follows:"

They abide in the stage of practicing the three refuges, the stage of following by faith, the stage of following by dharma, the stage of virtuous ordinary persons, the stage of training in the precepts, the stage of the eighth person, the stage of the srotāpanna, the stage of the sakṛdāgāmin, the stage of the anāgāmin, and the stage of the arhat.
“World-Honored One!
How many stages of the Pratyekabuddha are there?
The Buddha said:
“There are ten stages of the Pratyekabuddha. They are: the stage of the equipment of manifold virtues;

the stage of self-awakening to profound dependent origination; the stage of awakening to the Four Noble Truths; the stage of supreme, profound, and sharp wisdom; the stage of the Eightfold Noble Path; the stage of knowing the realm of phenomena, the realm of space, and the realm of sentient beings; the stage of realizing cessation; the stage of the six supernormal powers; the stage of entry into the subtle and wondrous; and the stage of attenuated habitual tendencies.”
“World-Honored One!
How many bodhisattva stages are there?
The Buddha said:
“There are ten bodhisattva stages,

namely: the Stage of Joy, the Immaculate Stage, the Luminous Stage, the Radiant Stage, the Extremely Difficult to Conquer Stage, the Manifest Stage, the Far-Reaching Stage, the Immovable Stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, and the Cloud of Dharma Stage.”
“World-Honored One!
From what do all things within their own respective realms arise?
The Buddha said:
“O Noble Being!
From the stage of the Tathāgata, all one’s own stages arise.
“World-Honored One!”
"What is the distinction between the various liberations?
The Buddha said,
"What is the distinction between river water and the water of the great ocean?"
“World-Honored One!
There is a difference in size between river water and ocean water.
The Buddha said:
"So it is, so it is, O noble son! The liberation of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas is like the water of a river; the liberation of a Tathāgata is like the water of the great ocean."
“World-Honored One!
Do not all great rivers, small streams, and every flow of water enter the ocean?
The Buddha said:
"It is so, it is so; it is just as you have said.

Whether it be the Dharma of the Śrāvakas, the Dharma of the Pratyekabuddhas, the Dharma of the Bodhisattvas, or the Dharma of the Buddhas, all equally enter the ocean of wisdom, the Vairocana-treasury."
“World-Honored One!
We pray that you will manifest the first stage (*bhūmi*) of a Tathāgata currently abiding; for the domain of a Tathāgata is not known by any bodhisattvas, much less by śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.”
At that time, the World-Honored One manifested his own buddha-field, named "Inconceivable Adornment of Boundless Asaṃkhyeya Merit Jeweled Canopies.

That land was vast and expansive, such that as many buddha-fields as there are atoms in three-thousandfold great thousandfold world-systems equaling the sands of ten million nayutas of Ganges Rivers were each entirely contained within this sovereign buddha-field of "Inconceivable Adornment of Boundless Asaṃkhyeya Merit Jeweled Canopies."

In that buddha-field, the kings of mountains—Mount Meru, Sumeru, Mahāmeru, and all the Black Mountains—as well as rivers, seas, streams, hills, precipices, earth, stones, pebbles, filth, various insects, mire, and impurities; the hells, the animal realm, and the world of Yama’s ghosts; the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans; and even the former adornments of the buddha-fields—all these are entirely removed. The ground becomes level like the palm of a hand, composed of lapis lazuli.

In the center of the Buddha-field is a ground of deep blue jewels, rising from the adamantine base as a sovereign, most excellent, and wondrously adorned *aśoka* Bodhi tree king. Composed of the seven treasures, it stands preeminent and resplendent, reaching a height equal to worlds as numerous as the atoms within immeasurable *Gaṅgā*-sands of Buddha-fields, its broad canopy likewise extending that far.

Adorned with various precious leaves, flowers, and fruits, its branches and trunks were all composed of exquisite jewels; the light of mani gems, various rare treasures, and non-empty jewel filaments shone forth brilliantly. Necklaces of pearls, jeweled necklaces, silk pendants, and nets of bells hung down and covered it, while the radiance of flowing lightning-garlands, golden light, mani gems, sapphire, crystal, sun-loved, and moon-loved gems illuminated it.

Furthermore, fragrances such as agallochum, tagara, black agallochum, tamāla leaves, kālānusāri, uragasāra sandalwood, and gośīrṣa sandalwood—various supreme, wondrous, and pleasing scents—pervaded the buddha-field; the sounds of various musical instruments flowed forth, and a rain of all kinds of jewels fell throughout all worlds.
To the east of the Bodhi tree is the King of Bodhi Pools, named Immaculate Supreme Purity.

This pool is vast and immeasurable, equal in extent to worlds as numerous as the atoms within three thousand great thousandfold world-systems, each as vast as the sands of the Ganges. It is composed of the seven precious jewels and filled with water possessing the eight qualities. Its bottom is strewn with Jāmbūnada gold sand, and its four corners and four stairways are inlaid with various jewels; diverse jeweled couches and balustrades are fully provided and arranged all around it.

Within the Bodhi-pool there is a king of bodhi-lotuses named "Exquisitely Blossoming Face," equal in magnitude to worlds as numerous as the atoms within immeasurable, vast trichiliocosms like the sands of the Ganges. Its petals are adorned with countless koṭis, nayutas, and hundreds of thousands of varieties of the seven precious jewels; they are supple, lustrous, subtle, fragrant, and pure.

Upon the lotus pedestal was the Bodhi Palace King, named Boundless Adornment. It was immeasurably high and wide, equal in size to worlds as numerous as the atoms within three thousandfold great thousandfold world-systems as many as the sands of the Ganges. Composed of the seven precious jewels, it was supremely exquisite and its spiritual powers were brilliantly manifest, surpassing the previous Palace of Jewel Adornments by billions of times.
It is just as when a firefly is set against the solar disc; likewise, the various lights of the Palace Adorned with Jewels do not appear before the Palace of Bodhi.

The King of the Palace of Bodhi possesses boundless, supreme, and wondrous adornments, and its supernatural radiance blazes so intensely that the sun and moon cease their shining and lose their majestic luster. The light of all the Śakras, Brahmās, and gods of the Pure Abodes is entirely eclipsed, and their magnificent splendors no longer appear.

Within the Bodhi Hall was the Great Bodhi Lion Throne King, named Adorned with the Non-Void Stamen of Sublime Radiance. The dimensions of that throne—its height and breadth—were perfectly equal, as vast as worlds containing atoms from immeasurable *nayuta* of Ganges-sand worlds. It was adorned all around with the most exquisite colors and various kinds of the seven precious gems, and draped with subtle celestial silks such as Kāśika, Vaidūrya, and Kauseya, which were spread out and hung down.

The Buddha Śākyamuni—known as the Tathāgata King of Sun and Moon Wisdom Light, Sovereign of the Supreme Treasury of Supernatural Powers, the Mass of Merit of Wondrous Marks and the Perfect Halo Adorned with a Vaiḍūrya Field, the Banner of the Vairocana-Treasury, the Moon-Illuminating Stainless Radiance Merit-Flower Free-from-Dye—sat upon the Bodhi lion throne, his body as vast as the three-thousandfold world system containing as many atoms as there are in hundreds of koṭis of Ganges-sands of buddha-fields.

His physical form was perfectly complete, adorned with the thirty-two major marks and eighty minor characteristics; his halo was magnificent, and his sublime hair and unsurpassed crown were such that none could behold them.

Subtle, wondrous, radiant, and pure, they were like sunlight entering a bright mirror. He did not possess a body of flesh, blood, bone, or marrow, but was supremely exquisite and pure, with a brilliant luster like Jāmbūnada gold, as clear and translucent as lapis lazuli, sapphire, and other precious gems.

Having eradicated all subtle habitual tendencies, the Greatly Awakened World-Honored One is endowed with all excellences and is the Teacher of All-Knowledge; he possesses unimpeded mastery over all phenomena, is the unsurpassed deliverer of all beings, the supreme one of great compassion, the supreme person, the lion among men, and has reached the ultimate exhaustion of the outflows.

His adamantine body is adorned with a hundred merits; he possesses the ten powers of a Buddha, a great mass of merit, the four fearlessnesses, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. He roars the true lion’s roar, and his lifespan is boundless, free from aging or decay.

In a pure land, one realizes perfect enlightenment (sambodhi), attains one's own true nature and one's own light, and is surrounded by a multitude of immeasurable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have arisen through transformation and offer worship.

Each of those bodhisattvas, according to their own respective physical appearance and requirements, manifested within the lotus pedestals of the jewel ponds, inside the jeweled palaces, beneath the trees of various jewels, and upon lion thrones, adorned with all the appropriate ornaments as befits a Buddha.

This Buddha-world is adorned with merit, supremely wonderful and pure; the Buddha’s body and his assembly are supremely wonderful and pure; the eon is supreme and pure, and the eon is named Great Eon King.
The measure of those kalpas and the measure of their adornments are both inexpressible.
The extent of the Buddha-field and the realm of the Tathāgata transcend all language and have no fixed location; thus, realizing *samyak-saṃbodhi* is called "dwelling in the stage of the Tathāgata."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sāgaravaradharagambhīravikrīḍitājñānābhijña, saying:
"Noble Son! Do you see this magnificent display of the Tathāgata?"
The Bodhisattva Sāgaravaradharagambhīravikrīḍitājñānābhijña said:
“Indeed, I have seen it,
World-Honored One!”
“I have seen it, Sugata!
the Buddha said.

“O Noble One! Most supreme, profound, and difficult to discern is the wisdom of the light of Vipula, which constitutes the first stage of a Tathāgata; when a Buddha dwells in this stage, his supernormal powers are such as these.”

Just as I now manifest these supernatural powers, so too does the Tathāgata—named Decided-Vow-Adornment-Merit-Banner-Field-One-Umbrella-Sound-Sovereign-Majesty-King-Jeweled-Accumulation-Vairocana-Treasury-Superior-Aspect-Arisen-Uṣṇīṣa-Pure-Face-Akṣobhya-Uninterrupted-Light—manifest such great supernatural powers in the world-system of Joy, where he is venerated by gods and humans.

The Tathāgata Maṇirājaprabhāsa-vijaya-tejo-lakṣaṇa-padmasambhava-sarvaguṇavibhūṣita, the Tathāgata Anantaprabha, the Tathāgata Padmavikāsana-pūrvendrarāja-nāgeśvara-rāja, the Tathāgata Ratnākara, and other Buddhas such as these, as well as all other Buddhas of the present and future who dwell in supreme, wondrous, and pure lands—know that they all abide in the stage of Buddhahood.
The Bodhisattva Sāgaravaradharagambhīravikrīḍitājñānābhijña addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
To all Buddhas of the present and the future!”
“Do those who attain perfect enlightenment in an age of five corruptions not all likewise attain the stage of a Tathāgata?
The Buddha said,
“Virtuous One!”

Through their skillful means and great compassion, the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas behold all sentient beings deeply submerged within the three realms of existence, entangled in the net of ignorance and craving, with their faculties of faith impaired by false views and perversions. Having fallen into the midst of boundless suffering, these beings wander through the six destinies; drifting and sinking within the realm of sentient beings since beginningless time, they do not know its origin. They do not know the Buddha, nor the Buddha’s Dharma, nor the Bodhisattva’s Dharma, and are thus unable to know, as it truly is, the path of deliverance.

Out of compassion for these sentient beings, the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas manifest through transformation bodies (*nirmāṇakāya*) by taking birth in evil lands, or they display their passing away and transition;
or they manifest dwelling in the womb and growing up, enjoying the pleasures of youth amidst palace maidens and music;

or they manifest weariness with the world, departing to practice austerities, proceeding to the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), subduing the armies of Māra, realizing *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, being exhorted to preach the Dharma, turning the Great Wheel of Dharma, crushing the arguments of non-Buddhists, refuting and destroying false teachings, and guiding those who have strayed into evil and heterodoxy so that they may return to the correct path.

Even unto manifesting a short lifespan and the Great Parinirvāṇa, he uses the power of samādhi to crush his bodily members into pieces like mustard seeds, establishing koṭis of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of reliquary stūpas. Immeasurable devas, nāgas, and even humans and non-humans offer extraordinary, sincere, and respectful worship;
some leave the household life within the Teaching to receive the Dharma and practice it, while others plant the seeds for Buddhahood to emerge from the ocean of birth and death.
"O Noble One!
In this way, the subtle and wondrous dharma-nature of all Buddhas rescues sentient beings from the boundless, asaṃkhyeya ocean of suffering in saṃsāra;

through the skillful means of their supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), they manifest birth in impure lands, or, through the skillful means of a bodhisattva’s supernormal powers, they manifest as bodhisattvas and assemblies of bodhisattvas."
The Bodhisattva Sāgaravaradharagambhīravikrīḍitajñānābhijña said:
“World-Honored One!
How many bodies does the Tathāgata possess?”
The Buddha said:
"O Noble One! Briefly stated, there are three aspects of the Tathāgata’s body."
That is to say:
the body of full enjoyment, the transformation body, and the essential body.
“World-Honored One! [What is the meaning of this?]”
"What is the Tathāgata’s body of fulfilled requisites?
The Buddha said, "Noble son!"
That you now see me is the Tathāgata’s body of complete enjoyment (*saṃbhogakāya*).

Furthermore, you should know that all other Buddhas who have realized, are realizing, or will realize the state of a Samyaksaṃbuddha in pure lands are likewise the Tathāgata’s bodies of complete enjoyment.
“World-Honored One!
What is the transformation body (nirmāṇakāya) of the Tathāgata? The Buddha said:

“O Noble One! Just as the Buddhas Bala-atikrānta-vīra, Māra-vidhvamsana, Mahākaruṇā-cintin, and all other Buddhas appear in defiled lands to realize the state of a Samyaksambuddha—having realized it, or yet to realize it—and manifest passing away, the abiding of the assembly of dharmas during the True Dharma and Semblance Dharma periods, and even manifest the complete disappearance and extinction of all Buddha-dharmas.”
"Virtuous ones!
You must not take this as being real. Why is that?"
"One should know that all such dharmas are manifested through the skillful means of great compassion according to what is appropriate.
"World-Honored One!
Why is the Dharma-body of the Tathāgata also called the Svabhāvakāya (Self-nature Body)?"
The Buddha said: "O Noble Being!

The Dharma-body is without form and without manifestation; it is unimpeded and without likeness; it is non-representational and without abiding; it is without dependence and without grasping; it neither ceases nor arises, and it is beyond all analogy."
Thus it is, O Noble One!
The self-nature body of the Tathāgata is ineffable;

the body of the Tathāgata is the Dharma-body, the Wisdom-body, the Unequaled-body, the Peerless-body, the Vairocana-body, the Space-body, the Uninterrupted-body, the Indestructible-body, the Infinite-body, the Supreme-body, the Reality-body, the Incomparable-body, and the Self-nature-body.
“World-Honored One!
If the Tathāgata’s self-nature body is without form, without manifestation, and even beyond verbal expression, would this not be a characteristic of annihilation?”
The Buddha said:
"Virtuous One! What do you think?"
“Is the realm of space something that is severed, or is it something that exists?
“World-Honored One! [he asked.]
The realm of space is neither annihilated nor existent. Why is this?
If the realm of space were annihilated, there would be no unimpeded activity.
If it were existent, there would be a physical entity with accumulated dimensions.
World-Honored One!
Therefore, the space element is neither annihilated nor existent, but is omnipresent throughout all things.
The Buddha said:
"Virtuous one! Excellent, excellent!"
It is so, it is so. The Tathāgata’s self-nature body is neither annihilated nor existent. Why is this?
"O Noble One!
If the self-nature body of the Tathāgata were subject to cessation, then there would be no appearance of Buddhas in the world to manifest immeasurable supernatural powers and perform great benefits.

If it were something that exists, then it would have a locus of accumulation that could be grasped or relinquished; it would be no different from all Brahmins and ordinary worldlings, and there would be no sequence of before and after, as everyone would attain Buddhahood simultaneously."
"Therefore, the Tathāgata’s body of intrinsic nature is neither annihilated nor existent, yet it performs all the buddha-works for all sentient beings.
"World-Honored One!
Among making offerings to the Tathāgata’s body of intrinsic nature, the body of fulfilled resources, and the transformation body, which yields the greater merit?"
The Buddha said:
"Virtuous One! If one makes an offering to the body of a single Tathāgata, that is equivalent to making an offering to the bodies of all Tathāgatas."
Why is this? All light is capable of dispelling darkness and providing illumination; there is no light that coexists with darkness.
Thus it is, O noble son!

Whosoever makes offerings to any of the Tathāgata’s bodies, their roots of goodness shall all become vast, eliminating all the accumulated darkness of ignorance and illuminating the path to nirvāṇa and liberation; no obscurations or darkness shall ever accompany them.
“World-Honored One!
We pray that you will reveal the second stage of the Tathāgata.
The Buddha said:
“Noble sir! Are you able to see?
“World-Honored One!”
"I hope to behold the marks of his appearance.

Thereupon, the Buddha emitted the Light of Non-nature from a single pore, which shone universally throughout unspeakably many buddha-fields, such that no forms whatsoever appeared and all signs were entirely absent.
The Buddha asked the bodhisattvas,
"What do you see now? At that time,
the bodhisattvas all addressed the Buddha, saying:
"We see only light; nothing else is seen.
The Buddha said, "As for the light you all see, what is that light like?"
The bodhisattvas said:
"In as many buddha-fields as there are atoms in immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Ganges-sands of buddha-fields, we see only a single field of universal light."
When he had spoken thus, the Buddha withdrew his net of light, and all the buddha-fields returned to their former state.
The Buddha addressed the bodhisattvas:
"If you cannot even recognize or comprehend two of the Tathāgata’s stages, how much less can you explain or perceive the Tathāgata’s third stage up to the tenth?"
O noble sons!

It is like the sun and moon, by whose radiance sentient beings sustain themselves and bring forth life; through the movement of the sun and moon, there come day and night, the *pakṣa*, month, year, *lava*, *muhūrta*, the seasons, and the times, which cause sentient beings to have knowledge [of them].
Yet sentient beings perceive only the light and forms of the sun and moon palaces; they are unable to see the physical bodies of the sun and moon in their entirety.

O noble sons! In this same way, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, nurtures all sentient beings. Because of the Tathāgata, sentient beings come to know what is wholesome and unwholesome, what is mundane and supramundane, and what is with outflows and without outflows. Having known these, they practice according to reality and thereby cross over the wilderness of the manifold sufferings of birth and death.

Yet all sentient beings are unable to see the Tathāgata’s body, which is endowed with the perfection of all requisites; they see only the Tathāgata’s great compassion, spiritual power, skillful means, and manifested transformations.
"O noble sons!
You should know that the stage of the Tathāgata transcends all sounds and speech; I now speak of it merely by means of names!
At that time, the Bodhisattva Sāgaravaradharagambhīravikrīḍitājñānābhijña addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Who is able to cross over and transcend all evil paths?
The Buddha said:
“O Noble Being!

This is the Dharma-gate of the Mahāyāna for realizing the Tathāgata’s ten stages, which enters the most supreme and profound Vairocana-treasury of the wisdom that encompasses the realm of all Buddhas.”

If one hears it, and having heard it, believes it deeply; and having believed it, receives and upholds it, recites and studies it, copies and writes it, explains it to others, and widely disseminates it—or even if one merely holds the name of this Dharma-gate—all such persons shall transcend all the grounds of suffering in the various evil realms.
“World-Honored One!
Who gives rise to the bodhicitta?
The Buddha said:
“O Noble One! Receive and uphold this Dharma-gate; even those who merely hold its name shall give rise to the bodhicitta.
“World-Honored One! [he replied.]
"Who practices the bodhisattva path?
The Buddha said, "O Noble One!"
"One who upholds this Dharma-gate practices the bodhisattva conduct.
"World-Honored One!
Who is able to fulfill the six pāramitās with little exertion?"
The Buddha said:
"O Noble Being!
Those who uphold this Dharma-gate."
“World-Honored One!
Who is with the Buddha?
The Buddha said:
“Those who hear this Dharma-gate.
“World-Honored One!
Who will be able to easily receive the prediction [of enlightenment]?”
The Buddha said:
"Virtuous one! You who uphold this profound secret of the Tathāgata."
“World-Honored One!
Who acts as the great guide for all sentient beings?
The Buddha said:
“O Noble One! You who uphold this Tathāgatagarbha.
“World-Honored One!”
"Who is the Son of the Buddha?
The Buddha said, "O Noble One!"
"One who has deep faith in this dharma-gate.
"World-Honored One!
Who attains all the bodhisattva stages?"
The Buddha said:
"Noble son! Listen to this Dharma-gate."
“World-Honored One!
Who attains all Buddha-dharmas?
The Buddha said:
“O Noble Being!
One should honor and revere this torch of the Dharma.
“World-Honored One!”
"Who would know the vehicle of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas and yet not cross over by means of that vehicle?
The Buddha said, "Noble son!"
"Those who practice this treasury of the True Dharma—
World-Honored One,
what should this sutra be named?"
"How should it be upheld?
The Buddha said, "O Noble One!"
This Dharma door is named "Realization and Accordance with the Mahāyāna," and it is also named "Entering the Realm of Wisdom of All Buddhas: the Vairocana Treasury.
You should uphold it thus.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"If you wish to realize the Buddha’s Bodhi, The unsurpassed, vast, supreme, and true path;
To open the inconceivable, most excellent wisdom, And turn the holy, untainted, wondrous Wheel of Dharma;..."
Wishing to plant the banner of Dharma and beat the drum of Dharma, To blaze the great torch of Dharma and blow the conch of Dharma;
Wishing to shatter ignorance with the light of wisdom, And liberate sentient beings within the sphere of awakening and gnosis;
Wishing to subdue the armies of Māra and make offerings to the Buddha, With the supreme radiance illuminating all things.
With wisdom unstained and unattached to worldly dharmas, one cultivates the pure land for the benefit of sentient beings;
all should listen to and uphold this precious sutra, copying it, reading and reciting it, and widely disseminating it—
proclaiming and contemplating the supreme treasury of the Buddhas, the profound and wondrous stage of all Tathāgatas.

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaravaradharagambhīravicaya-jñānābhijña, together with the assembly of all Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, having heard what the Buddha taught, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
Sūtra on Realizing and Accordance with the Mahāyāna, Scroll II, Part B.
